We need propose a 5-step retrosynthesis route. Use protecting group steps, HWE, DIBAL-H, etc. We need to construct JSON tree with reactions and children (precursors). We need to select appropriate template IDs. We can search for templates matching each transformation. Let's identify steps backwards from target.

Target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Looks like a polyunsaturated chain with a terminal carboxylic acid (C(O)=O) attached to a conjugated diene chain attached to a cyclic sugar-like core with an ether side chain.

Probably retrosynthesis: 1) Deprotect TBS group? The target has free hydroxyls (maybe one is protected originally). The target has an ether O[C@@H]... maybe that is a protected group? Actually O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C) is an O-alkyl linking to the cyclic core. Could be a silyl ether originally protected then deprotected.

We need 5 steps. Could be:

Step5 (forward) = deprotection of TBS to give free OH. So retrosynthetic step: add TBS protecting group to one OH.

Step4 (forward) = Still-Gennari HWE to form Z-alkene linking the side chain (C=C(CO)/C) maybe from aldehyde and phosphonate.

Step3 (forward) = DIBAL-H reduction of ester to aldehyde.

Step2 (forward) = oxidation of primary alcohol to carboxylic acid? Actually target has carboxylic acid at end of chain. Could be formed from oxidation of aldehyde after HWE? Wait HWE forms double bond and retains carbonyl of phosphonate? Actually HWE forms alkene and leaves a carbonyl (ester) from phosphonate? In Still-Gennari, you get (Z)-alkene with an ester group attached (the phosphonate becomes an ester). So the terminal carboxylic acid could be derived from that ester after hydrolysis. So step2 could be hydrolysis of ester to acid.

Step1 (forward) = maybe start from simple building blocks: a protected sugar core and a phosphonate.

But we need 5 reactions total. Let's outline retrosynthesis:

Target (T) -> (Step5 reverse) TBS-protected intermediate (I5) where the free OH is protected as O-TBS.

Identify which OH is protected: The molecule has two OH groups: one on the cyclic core (O[C@H]1...), and one on side chain (C=C(CO)/C) includes CH2OH? Actually /C=C(CO)/C indicates a double bond with a CHO? Wait (C=C(CO)/C) means a double bond where one carbon attached to CO (aldehyde?) Actually CO is carbonyl? In SMILES, CO is methanol? "CO" is methoxy? Actually "CO" is carbon attached to O (i.e., -CH2-O?). Wait "CO" is carbon attached to O (C-O). So C=C(CO)/C means a double bond carbon attached to CO (i.e., -CH= C( -CH2O ) -). So side chain has a primary alcohol (CH2O). So there is an alcohol there.

Thus we have two alcohols: the cyclic OH and the side chain CH2OH. Likely one is protected as TBS.

So I5: protect side chain CH2OH as TBS.

Thus reaction: TBSCl + imidazole -> TBS ether.

We need template ID for TBS protection. Let's search.
